hook.line: Tomás's emails now sound like Vale's bank, and this is the reason: Colombian formal writing loves *me permito*, roughly "I take the liberty of".
hook.es: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
hook.en: I hereby inform you that your application has been approved. (formal)

examples.es: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
examples.en: I hereby inform you that your application has been approved. (formal)

examples.es: En respuesta a su anuncio, me permito presentar mi candidatura al cargo de analista.
examples.en: In response to your advertisement, I take the liberty of applying for the post of analyst.

examples.es: Nos permitimos invitarlos a la inauguración del café.
examples.en: We take the liberty of inviting you all to the opening of the café.

examples.es: Me permito solicitar una cita con el alcalde.
examples.en: I take the liberty of requesting an appointment with the mayor.

examples.es: Permítame presentarle a Vale, nuestra pastelera.
examples.en: Allow me to introduce Vale to you, our pastry chef. (formal)

examples.es: Me permito recordarle que la reunión es el lunes.
examples.en: I take the liberty of reminding you that the meeting is on Monday. (formal)

rule:
*Me permito* + infinitive is the polite way to say what a letter is doing: informing, requesting, applying. Literally it is "I allow myself to", but it is ritual courtesy, not real permission.

English usually just says "I am writing to inform you". For a team or a business it becomes *nos permitimos*. The command *permítame* ("allow me") works the same way.

Use it once, early, then go plain. Too many and the letter sounds like a bank: *Me permito informarle que…*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a courtesy formula: it softens the action rather than describing permission.

readAndPick.es: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
options: You inform me that my application was approved.
They let me know my application was approved.
I hereby inform you that your application was approved.

readAndPick.es: Nos permitimos invitarlos a la inauguración.
options: We take the liberty of inviting you all to the opening.
They take the liberty of inviting us to the opening.
I invite you to the opening.
You write to me again.
I take the liberty of writing to you again.
I allow you to write again.
Vale allows me to introduce you.
Let me tell Vale.
Allow me to introduce Vale to you.
I take the liberty of requesting an appointment.
They requested an appointment from me.
I allow you to request an appointment.

readAndPick.es: Nos permitimos recordarle que la reunión es el lunes.
options: We remind them that the meeting is on Monday.
We take the liberty of reminding you that the meeting is on Monday.
I take the liberty of reminding you that the meeting is on Monday.

options: The analyst offers me the post.
I allow the analyst to apply.
I take the liberty of applying for the post of analyst.
We take the liberty of making a complaint.
I take the liberty of making a complaint.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Me ___ informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.* (*permito* or *permite*) I hereby inform you (formal) that your application was approved.
yourTurn.answer: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
yourTurn.why: It is *I* who takes the liberty, so *permito*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Nos ___ invitarlos a la inauguración.* (*permitimos* or *permito*) We take the liberty of inviting you all to the opening.
yourTurn.answer: Nos permitimos invitarlos a la inauguración.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, in a letter: I take the liberty of requesting an appointment.
Say, for your team: We take the liberty of reminding you (formal) that the meeting is on Monday.
yourTurn.answer: Nos permitimos recordarle que la reunión es el lunes.
yourTurn.why: *Nos permitimos* + *recordarle* for one person you address as *usted*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Allow me to introduce Vale to you (formal).
yourTurn.why: *Permítame* is the polite command, and *a* goes before the person.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.*
yourTurn.answer: Nos permitimos informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *I*: *Nos permitimos solicitar una cita.*

pitfalls.wrong: Me permito a informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
pitfalls.right: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.

pitfalls.wrong: Permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
pitfalls.right: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
pitfalls.why: Without *me* it means "I allow", which is not the polite formula.

pitfalls.wrong: Me permito informarte que su solicitud fue aprobada.
pitfalls.right: Me permito informarle que su solicitud fue aprobada.
pitfalls.why: *Me permito* is formal, so it goes with *le* (*usted*), not *te*.
